definition: Autonomic networking follows the concept of Autonomic Computing, an initiative started by IBM in 2001.
details: Its ultimate aim is to create self-managing networks to overcome the rapidly growing complexity of the Internet and other networks and to enable their further growth, far beyond the size of today.

explainer.lead: Autonomic networking is the idea that a network should manage itself rather than depend entirely on people to handle every change. It applies IBM’s Autonomic Computing initiative, started in 2001, to networks whose growing size and complexity make manual management increasingly difficult.

tiers.eli5: Imagine roads that notice a traffic jam and change the signs and routes without waiting for someone to fix every problem. Autonomic networking wants computer networks to look after themselves in a similar way. This could help the Internet and other networks keep growing without becoming too complicated to manage.
tiers.practitioner: Apply the idea as a management loop: observe the network, decide whether its current state matches the desired behavior, adjust its operation, and check the result. The practical challenge is coordinating automatic decisions across a large, changing network rather than treating each device or incident in isolation.
tiers.paperLevel: Autonomic networking = application of Autonomic Computing principles to networking, with the objective of self-managing networks. It derives from IBM’s Autonomic Computing initiative, started in 2001, and addresses the management complexity that threatens the continued growth of the Internet and other networks.

explainer.example: A network detects that part of its infrastructure is congested, adjusts how traffic is handled, and then checks whether the congestion has eased, all without an operator manually performing each step.

usedIn.name: Internet operations
usedIn.detail: Self-management is intended to help control the Internet’s rapidly growing complexity.

usedIn.name: Large communication networks
usedIn.detail: The same approach aims to let other networks grow well beyond their present size without overwhelming manual management.

explainer.intuition: Instead of making administrators constantly translate every network change into manual actions, give the network the ability to manage its own operation. The goal is continued growth without a matching explosion in management effort.
howItWorks: Compare that condition with the desired behavior.
Choose management actions to close any gap.
Apply those actions to the network.
Continue observing so management can respond to further changes.
explainer.whyItMatters: Manual management becomes harder as networks grow larger and more complex. Self-managing behavior is intended to remove that barrier to the further growth of the Internet and other networks.
misconceptions: It is not simply a plan to build larger networks; it concerns how those networks manage themselves.
A single automated task does not by itself make an entire network autonomic.

nodes.label: Management decision
nodes.note: Select actions for the desired behavior

diagram.caption: Autonomic networking closes the loop between observing a network and changing how it operates.
